tagline: OV-099 — second operational Shuttle. Lost 73s after launch on STS-51-L (1986-01-28) with all seven crew including teacher Christa McAuliffe
dispatch: Challenger, OV-099, was the fleet's early workhorse and the site of its first catastrophe. It flew the program's first spacewalk and carried the first American woman, Sally Ride, to orbit. On 28 January 1986, launching in unusually cold weather, a rubber seal in one of its solid boosters — stiffened by the cold, a failure mode engineers had warned of — gave way, and the vehicle broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff. All seven aboard died. The disaster grounded the fleet for nearly three years and exposed a management culture that had flown past a known, flagged risk.
description: Built from a structural test article (STA-099) converted to flight after Enterprise was deemed too expensive to upgrade. First flew STS-6 (1983-04-04) carrying out the first Shuttle EVA. Flew 10 missions in total: STS-6, STS-7, STS-8, STS-41-B, STS-41-C, STS-41-G, STS-51-B, STS-51-F, STS-61-A, and final flight STS-51-L. On 1986-01-28, STS-51-L launched at unprecedented cold (−1 °C) — the right SRB's O-rings failed to seal, hot gas burned through the strut attaching the SRB to the external tank, and the orbiter broke apart at Max-Q (T+73s) at 14 km altitude. All seven crew perished including Sally Ride from her groundbreaking STS-7 mission. The Rogers Commission ground the Shuttle for 32 months and rewrote NASA's safety culture.
